Smarsh is seeking a Procurement Manager to lead and manage the procurement team, driving daily execution while helping translate strategic direction into action.

This role will manage a team spanning vendor procurement, systems/vendor analysis, and strategic sourcing, and will own two related but distinct work streams: procurement process execution and vendor management, including a new vendor review process built in partnership with InfoSec and Legal.

This is a people-management and execution-focused role that drives the direction into daily team operations and results, helping move Smarsh toward a more mature, enterprise-grade procurement process. What will you do?

· Directly manage and develop the procurement team, including workload distribution, coaching, and performance management
· Translate the procurement strategy and direction set by leadership into concrete team priorities, processes, and daily execution
· Own current-state PO and procurement workflow execution across Jira and NetSuite
· Evaluate and help define the next direction for procurement tooling — including a potential Jira-to-NetSuite integration, a NetSuite upgrade to natively support procurement, or the adoption of third-party procurement tooling.
· Drive process documentation and continuous improvement across procurement workflows (e.g. PO fast-track procedures, vendor bill/PO best practices)
· Serve as an escalation point for day-to-day procurement issues, removing blockers for the team
· Report on team performance, procurement metrics, and process health to leadership

s.h: Vendor Management (separated from core procurement process)
s.t:

· Build and formalize a vendor review process covering onboarding, ongoing risk assessment, and offboarding
· Build and define partnerships with InfoSec and Legal to establish multi-lane, requirements-based review paths depending on purchase type (e.g. software vs. services vs. hardware) and vendor status (new vs. existing/renewal)
· Define escalation and review criteria that scale review rigor to risk (e.g. data access, spend threshold, contract type) rather than applying a single process to every vendor
· Support Smarsh 's broader move toward a more mature, enterprise-grade procurement process by ensuring vendor governance keeps pace with sourcing and tooling changes
What will you bring?
5+ years of experience in procurement, sourcing, or vendor management, with 2+ years in a people management role
Demonstrated experience building or maturing a vendor review/risk process, ideally in partnership with InfoSec and/or Legal
Experience driving process improvement and documentation in a procurement or operations function
Strong ability to translate high-level strategic direction into team execution
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills across Finance, IT, InfoSec, Legal, and vendor-facing functions.
Experience leading or contributing to a procurement systems evaluation or migration (e.g. build vs. buy, tooling RFP) is preferred.
Background in IT/technology vendor procurement specifically is preferred.
Experience designing risk-tiered or multi-lane vendor review frameworks is preferred.
Experience supporting compliance or audit needs tied to procurement (e.g. SOC 2, vendor risk)is preferred.

We're looking for a Senior Inventory Planner to own product launch planning and post-launch replenishment execution for Quince's UK and EU expansion. This is not a steady-state replen role. It's the planner who decides how deep we go on new products at launch, then operates the day-to-day to make sure those products actually land on time and scale well.
You'll size initial launch buys for products dropping into the UK and EU at a weekly cadence, often with little or no local demand history, by triangulating from Quince overall performance, comparable products, comparable markets, lead-time realities, and informed judgement.

Once products are live, you'll act on early sell-through signals and trigger replenishment decisions fast, pulling forward, doubling down on winners, cutting losses on losers, and adjusting the next launch wave based on what the market is teaching us.
This role sits at the heart of Quince's International expansion. Working alongside a planning and automation counterpart who owns the underlying forecasting models and demand sensing, you'll be the operator who turns those signals into real-world action.

Sizing the buys, placing the POs, working the relationships, and getting product in the warehouse on time. Your edge is judgement, speed, and the trust you build with the people who make execution actually happen.

You'll be operating where the tooling is still being built around you, the data is thinner than you'd like, and the answer often has to be reasoned from first principles. Comfort operating in a dynamic environment isn't a nice-to-have, it's the job.
The ideal candidate has lived this work before. Sizing launch buys, executing replenishment decisions, working POs through to landing at a DTC or M2C that moves quickly and has international exposure. You're a builder of relationships first and a builder of spreadsheets second.

You're energized by placing well-reasoned bets under uncertainty, by getting product to land on time when it shouldn't have, and by the trust you accumulate with vendors and cross-functional partners over time. You communicate constraints bluntly but constructively.

You don't wait for perfect data, and you don't let a winning product sit understocked while you wait for statistical significance.
Success in This Role Means
Product launch buys are sized well. Products that are market winners aren't crippled by stockouts and losers don't tie up working capital you can't recover.
Post-launch product replenishment decisions are fast and well judged. Safety stock and WOS is controlled and refreshed as market signals mature. Winning products scale into demand, losing products get cut before they bleed.
Forecast accuracy improves measurably on new products, even where historical data is thin.
POs land on time, in full, and any deviation is known, flagged, and managed proactively
Merch, sourcing, production partners, vendors, and your peer planners in other geographies trust you completely. You're the person they pick up the phone for, the one whose word on a PO they take to the bank, the one they share early intelligence with.
Inventory turns improve as the UK and EU business scales
The launch and replen frameworks you build for the UK don't just serve the UK today. They become the blueprint for how Quince plans every new market launch that comes next.

Own end-to-end launch planning for new products entering the UK and EU markets. Size the initial buy, sequence against lead times and launch dates, and translate it into clean PO recommendations
Take forecasting models, demand signals, and algorithmic recommendations developed by the team and operationalize them. Apply judgement on top, raise issues when the model is wrong, and feed real-world execution learnings back to improve the models
Manage POs end-to-end. Generate, adjust, expedite, and follow up with vendors and internal stakeholders to ensure on-time, in-full delivery against launch dates
Partner closely with merchandising on assortment and launch calendars, and with sourcing and production on lead times, capacity, vendor allocation, and PO execution. These are your primary day-to-day partners
Build and nurture strong working relationships with partners directly. Communicate constraints clearly, hold them accountable to commitments, escalate constructively when needed, and become the partner they prioritize when capacity is tight
Work as part of a global planning community. Share intelligence with planning counterparts in the US and other geographies, lift and adapt their analogs and learnings into UK and EU plans, and escalate cross-market issues quickly
Build and maintain the operational artifacts (trackers, dashboards, status notes) that give the rest of the business confidence in launch readiness and post-launch performance
